query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered suitable for thin-film use, and its expense favors applying it as a protective coating on conventional metals rather than using it in bulk. Earlier studies examined room-temperature wear behavior in relation to coating–substrate combinations, composition, and grain size, but largely addressed the alloy itself or a limited thermal regime rather than the overall wear response of a coating across different temperatures. Under the constraints that FeNiCrCoCu remains a thin protective coating and that high-temperature wear is the target application, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs its overall wear resistance and why? Specify an intervention relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, state the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, connect the hypothesis to prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Thermal pre-oxidation treatment of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings induces the formation of a protective, finely dispersed grain-boundary oxide phase that improves high-temperature wear resistance by reducing coating/substrate delamination and friction.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating on a conventional metal substrate
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled high-temperature oxidative annealing (thermal pre-oxidation treatment) to promote the formation of a stable oxide network at the grain boundaries
generation.conditions: Wear testing conducted in ambient atmosphere under a constant normal load (e.g., 20 N) over a temperature range from room temperature (25°C) to approximately 600°C
generation.structural_mediator: Grain-boundary oxide phase network formed during the pre-oxidation treatment
generation.mechanism: The pre-formed oxide phase acts to stabilize the coating microstructure at elevated temperatures by reducing thermal stress and inhibiting crack propagation and delamination. Additionally, the oxide may impart a lubricious effect that lowers friction during sliding wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to as-deposited coatings, the thermally pre-oxidized coatings will display lower wear rates and reduced coefficients of friction at high temperatures (especially near 600°C). Microscopic analysis should reveal a coherent oxide network at grain boundaries that correlates with the improved wear performance.
generation.baseline: As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating without any thermal pre-oxidation
generation.boundary: This effect is expected to hold within the tested temperature range (25°C to 600°C) under the specified normal load in ambient air. The hypothesis may not apply if the test conditions (e.g., load, temperature, or atmosphere) fall outside these bounds.
generation.uncertainty: The degree of wear improvement (quantitative reduction in wear rate or friction) is uncertain, as it depends on the specifics of the oxidation kinetics and microstructural evolution during pre-treatment, which may be alloy- and process-parameter dependent.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set with as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coatings and one set treated with a controlled thermal pre-oxidation process. Subject both sets to systematic wear testing using a standardized tribometer under a constant 20 N normal load across temperatures ranging from 25°C to 600°C in ambient air. After testing, analyze the wear tracks and microstructure to determine the presence and coherence of a grain-boundary oxide phase.
measurements: Wear rate (via mass loss or volumetric analysis)
Microscopic characterization (e.g., SEM, TEM) to identify and assess the oxide phase at grain boundaries
Adhesion tests between the coating and substrate
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-oxidized coatings do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in wear rate and friction coefficient at elevated temperatures compared to the as-deposited coatings, or if post-test microstructural analysis fails to reveal the formation of a coherent grain-boundary oxide phase, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract WVTaTiCr x ( x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings were prepared on a 42-CrMo steel plate using laser cladding. The purpose of this work is to investigate the effect of the Cr content on the microstructure and properties of the WVTaTiCr x coating. The morphologies and phase compositions of five coatings with different Cr contents were comparatively observed. In addition, the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coatings were also analyzed. As a result, with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined. All the coating is mainly composed of the BCC solid-solution phase, which promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase with the increase in Cr. The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating. The WVTaTiCr (Cr 1 ) exhibited superior mechanical properties, especially in terms of its exceptional hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance. Abstract In this study, the wear behaviour of a powder metallurgically produced AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 high-entropy alloy (HEAs) is investigated at elevated temperatures. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of inert gas atomised feedstock enables the production of dense bulk material. The microstructure evolution and phase formation are analysed. The high cooling rate in the atomisation process results in spherical powder with a microstructure comprising two finely distributed body-centred cubic phases. An additional phase with a complex crystal structure precipitates during SPS processing, while no coarsening of microstructural features occurs. The wear resistance under reciprocating wear conditions increases at elevated temperatures due to the formation of a protective oxide layer under atmospherical conditions. Additionally, the coefficient of friction (COF) slightly decreases with increasing temperature. SPS processing is suitable for the production of HEA bulk material. An increase in the wear resistance at elevated temperature enables high temperature applications of the HEA system AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 . chosen.technique: performing high-temperature oxidative annealing to pre-form protective oxide networks, followed by systematic high-temperature tribological evaluations using a standardized tribometer
chosen.conditions: Experiments conducted from 25°C to 600°C under a constant normal load (e.g., 20 N) and fixed sliding conditions in ambient air; the baseline condition is the as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating without any thermal pre-treatment
chosen.why: This approach fills the niche by directly probing the wear response over a broad temperature range. Prior studies focused only on room temperature and on the alloy itself; by intervening with a controlled thermal treatment that promotes grain boundary oxidation, the study tests the hypothesis that the formation of an adherent oxide phase improves wear resistance at high temperatures. Observing a reduction in wear rate and friction in the oxidized coatings—compared to the baseline—supports the hypothesis, while a lack of improvement or premature coating failure would falsify it.
